mutants.reason: With && the (RESP && ERR) term is never true, so beats_left, address and error-state data never update after an R handshake. Multi-beat reads never reach the last beat, so RLAST is never raised and the beat count and addresses are wrong.
WREADY is high in every state except WDAT (and in DRAIN). It is high before AW is accepted and low when W data is expected, which breaks WREADY gating and the W beat count.
The AWSIZE>2 check now sets w_aw_valid=1 instead of 0. Writes with unsupported size 3..7 are accepted and sent to APB instead of being drained and answered with SLVERR.
The REQ state advances on !i_req_ready. The write sequencer moves to WAIT before the APB controller accepts the beat, and it stalls once the controller accepts it. APB writes are lost or hang.
The WRAP alignment test is inverted. Legal aligned WRAP writes are rejected with SLVERR and no APB access, while unaligned ones are accepted.

req_ready is given when the APB FSM is not IDLE, not when it is IDLE. Payload capture needs req_ready in IDLE, so APB SETUP starts without a captured payload, and the sequencer handshake happens in the wrong phase.

The response (rsp_valid, data, err) is latched when the APB FSM is not in ACCESS but PREADY is high. PRDATA and PSLVERR are not captured at the true completion, so R and B responses are lost or wrong.

The W capture, beats_left decrement and address advance now fire when WDAT or wvalid is true. Data, strobes and address are captured or consumed without a W handshake, or in non-WDAT states, so PWDATA, PSTRB and the beat count are corrupted.

Line 165 is only the default assignment ahead of the case on reg_fsm_apb_current_state. Every case branch (SETUP, ACCESS and default) assigns o_apb_pwrite again, so the initial 1 never reaches the port.
The default of w_ar_valid becomes 0 and nothing sets it back to 1. Every read is treated as unsupported, so legal reads get SLVERR with no APB access.
Write transfers latch pwrite=0, so they appear on APB as reads. The write response goes to the read response path and the AXI write never completes correctly.
The default of o_axi_rvalid becomes 1 and is never cleared. RVALID is high in IDLE, REQ and WAIT and during reset, giving spurious R beats.
WREADY needs state==WDAT and state==DRAIN at once, which never happens. WREADY is never raised, so write data is never accepted and writes hang.

turn_rd is only read in the ctrl IDLE state. The controller leaves ACTRD only through i_rd_done, and then both versions clear turn_rd. The mutant also clears it early while waiting in ACTRD, but that value is never observed. The else-if write branch is not affected because rd_done never occurs outside ACTRD.
The APB start needs both read and write grants and requests at once, which never happens. APB SETUP never begins and every transfer hangs.

The beat counter and address update only on the last beat instead of on every non-last beat. Multi-beat reads do not advance the address or count, so the address sequence and RLAST position are wrong.
The read APB request valid is asserted in every state except REQ. The APB read is not requested in REQ, so legal reads stall or issue spurious requests.
The IDLE branch is inverted. Valid reads go to the ERR state (SLVERR beats, no APB) and invalid reads go to the APB REQ path.
rd_done fires on any R handshake or on RLAST alone. The owner is released after every beat, or before RREADY on the last beat, so another transaction can start mid-burst.
wr_ready stays 0 in IDLE, so the controller never moves GRW to ACTWR and never sees wr_done. After the first write the controller stays in GRW, the turn never flips, and reads are starved.

The invalid-WRAP test uses && instead of ||. WRAP with a bad length (not 2/4/8/16 beats) but aligned, or with a good length but unaligned, is now accepted instead of rejected. The bad-length case is an unsupported burst under the spec, so the mutant issues APB for it instead of SLVERR.
The write error is accumulated only when not in WAIT. rsp_valid only arrives in WAIT, so PSLVERR on APB writes is never recorded and BRESP is OKAY instead of SLVERR.
The AW beat count gets a 1 prefix, adding 256 to the 9-bit sum. The INCR total byte count for the 4-KiB check is wrong, so legal INCR writes are rejected as 4-KiB crossings.
DRAIN exits when the last-beat condition is false. The reject path leaves DRAIN right away and gives B before all AWLEN+1 W beats are drained, and the beat count goes wrong.
The cache check is now cache==0 && cache!=1. AWCACHE=0000 (legal) is rejected, and illegal values such as 0010 are accepted and sent to APB.
The turn bit is inverted, so AW wins the first tie after reset and the preference alternates the wrong way.
Payload capture requires the APB FSM not to be IDLE, but req_ready is only high in IDLE. Address, data, strobe and PPROT are never latched, so PADDR and PPROT stay 0.
wr_done fires as soon as BVALID is high, even without BREADY. The owner is released while B is still pending, so a new transaction can start during B backpressure.
In the idle/default branch PENABLE becomes 1 while PSEL is 0, so PENABLE is high without PSEL and in reset.
rd_ready stays 0 in IDLE, so the controller never leaves GRD to ACTRD and never sees rd_done. After the first read the controller stays in GRD, the turn never flips, and writes are starved.
PSEL is 0 during the ACCESS phase, so PENABLE is high without PSEL. The APB access phase is wrong.
The AR beat count gets a 1 prefix, adding 256. The INCR total byte count for the 4-KiB check is wrong, so legal INCR reads are rejected as 4-KiB crossings.

The invalid-WRAP test uses && instead of ||. WRAP writes with a bad length (not 2/4/8/16 beats) but aligned, or with a good length but unaligned, are now accepted instead of rejected. The bad-length case is an unsupported burst under the spec, so the mutant issues APB writes for it instead of SLVERR.
APB SETUP now starts whenever gnt_rd is high or rd_req_valid is high, even with no read request (for example during R backpressure, or in an unsupported read). This produces spurious APB transfers.
The WRAP next-address condition is inverted. A WRAP read wraps when it should not and increments across the wrap boundary, so the APB addresses are wrong.
RVALID/RLAST are driven in RESP and in every state except ERR. Unsupported reads never present their SLVERR beats, and RVALID is high in IDLE, REQ and WAIT.
